interest: This document provides valuable insight into pre-World War II Japanese strategic interest and covert intelligence gathering in Portugal's neutral Asian colonies, specifically Macau and Portuguese Timor, shortly before the outbreak of the Second Sino-Japanese War. Although the folder preserves only the 'List of Papers' docket sheet rather than the full despatches, it illustrates inter-allied intelligence sharing in the region, noting information passed by British Honorary Vice Consul F. J. Gellion to the U.S. Consulate General in Hong Kong. Furthermore, the cross-references to State Department decimal files 7536.94 (Japan-Portugal political relations) and 853f.6363 (petroleum concessions in Timor) demonstrate how American diplomats tracked the intersection of Japanese military espionage and oil resource ambitions in Southeast Asia and the Pacific.
overview: This file (U.S. State Department decimal file 894.20253E, File 507) consists of a single 'List of Papers' docket sheet indexing three despatches originating from the American Consulate General in Hong Kong between April and May 1937. Authored by Consul Howard Donovan, the underlying despatches monitor Japanese military, espionage, and propaganda activities in the Portuguese territories of Macau and Portuguese Timor on the eve of the Second Sino-Japanese War. The list details Despatch No. 518 reporting developments in Macau and Portuguese Timor, Despatch No. 523 communicating intelligence obtained from F. J. Gellion (the Honorary British Vice Consul at Macau), and Despatch No. 555 providing a textual correction substituting 'Timor' for 'Macao'. The sheet also records administrative routing to the Divisions of Far Eastern Affairs (FE) and Western European Affairs (WE), along with cross-reference notations to files 7536.94 and 853f.6363.

subfiles.about: A State Department List of Papers docket sheet indexing three despatches from Hong Kong concerning Japanese intelligence and military activities in Macau and Portuguese Timor in April and May 1937.
subfiles.summary: This 'List of Papers' sheet summarizes three incoming despatches (Nos. 518, 523, and 555) received from U.S. Consul Howard Donovan in Hong Kong between April and May 1937 regarding Japanese activities in Macau and Portuguese Timor. Despatch No. 518 reported on ongoing Japanese developments in the two Portuguese territories, while Despatch No. 523 transmitted supplementary intelligence provided by British Honorary Vice Consul F. J. Gellion in Macau. Despatch No. 555 forwarded a textual correction for Despatch No. 518, specifying that 'Macao' should read 'Timor' on page two. The docket sheet notes distribution to the Divisions of Far Eastern Affairs and Western European Affairs, with cross-references to decimal files 7536.94 and 853f.6363.
